name: Afghani
summary: The broad-leaflet drug cannabis traditionally grown in Afghanistan and neighbouring Pakistan and Central Asia, long used for hashish. Botanists group it apart from the narrow-leaflet drug types of South Asia, Africa and Latin America. Western breeders later used Afghan seed as the stocky, fast-flowering half of many hybrids. The name covers a regional population, not one fixed variety.

origin.place: Afghanistan and neighbouring Pakistan / Central Asia

evidence.note: Allozyme study: wide-leafleted drug accessions came from Afghanistan and Pakistan.
Classifies the Central Asian domesticate (Afghanistan, Pakistan, Turkestan) as var. afghanica.

sources.title: Genetic evidence for speciation in Cannabis (Cannabaceae) — K.W. Hillig, Genetic Resources and Crop Evolution 52:161–180 (2005)
